podcast.title: Definition by Jim Stafford (1981)
podcast.body: Musician Jim Stafford stated that novelty songs are almost impossible to define, but they should always be "new and refreshing." "It is almost impossible to define novelty songs but they should be new and refreshing."

podcast.title: Definition by Joshua Clover
podcast.body: Author and UC Davis English professor Joshua Clover described a novelty song as one with "something very exaggerated in its differences or difference from other songs of his genre," usually pop, but sometimes country or rock. This difference, he notes, dominates the song rather than merely distinguishing it. "A novelty song has something very exaggerated in its differences or difference from other songs of his genre."

podcast.title: Good Storytelling as a Requirement
podcast.body: Jim Stafford highlighted that the singer needs to tell a good story within the song for it to be effective. He cited Kenny Rogers' "The Gambler" as an example of strong narrative in a song. "The singer needs to tell a good story."

srcs.episode: Ep. 44 - Streaking, Werewolves, Sharks, & Drinking - 70s Novelty Songs

podcast.title: Humor as an Element
podcast.body: Humor is considered an important element, with songs being successful if funny or entertaining enough. However, humor can become stale or offensive over time, which is why novelty songs with staying power often come from artists with staying power. "I think that if a song is funny enough or entertaining enough it can become a hit."

podcast.title: Musically Interesting as a Requirement
podcast.body: Jim Stafford emphasized that for a novelty song to "have legs" and be heard repeatedly, the music itself must be interesting enough to support the lyrics. This implies that while the lyrics are often central to the novelty, the musical quality contributes to its longevity. "The music has to be interesting enough to support the lyrics."

podcast.title: Performance Challenges
podcast.body: Jim Stafford compared performing a musical joke to telling any other joke, noting that it's difficult if the audience already knows the punchline. His challenge was to write clever enough songs that people would want to listen to them more than once. "The problem about telling a musical joke is the same as telling any other joke you're dead if people stop you in the middle of it."
